Financial aid and awards
Each year, multiple scholarships, fellowships, prizes and bursaries are available to students in the Faculty of Science. We encourage you to also explore the research funding and awards available through the Faculty of Science.

Bursaries
Bursaries are awarded based on demonstrated financial need. In most cases, students must be registered in a minimum of 18 credit hours to be eligible. To be considered for bursaries offered at the University and Faculty of Science levels, students must submit the general bursary application. Bursary applications are available through Aurora in August. Please visit the financial aid and awards bursaries website for the annual application deadlines and additional information.

Faculty of Science Award for Excellence in Teaching Assistance
Teaching Assistants (TA) are valuable members of the Faculty of Science and play an important role in supporting the Faculty's teaching and learning mission. Some TAs go above and beyond their responsibilities to support their students and enhance their learning experience. Each year, two TAs in the Faculty of Science will be recognized for their outstanding contributions and excellence in teaching support.
⁠
The purpose of the award is to recognize outstanding TAs in the Faculty of Science and to motivate and inspire TAs to perform to the best of their ability.⁠
⁠
Awardees will receive $300 and recognition through the Faculty of Science website and social media.⁠
Nominations for the Winter Term are now closed.

Undergraduate scholarships and prizes
In most cases, applications are not required for these awards as they are based on academic achievement. Scholarships are generally offered to full-time continuing students, who are registered in a minimum of 24 credit hours.
Applications
The following undergraduate scholarships in the Faculty of Science require an application.
Students are also encouraged to visit the financial aid and awards website to find additional internal and external scholarships that require applications.
Prizes are awarded based on the highest academic standing or best performance in a particular course, program, competition or other area of achievement, with a minimum grade point average requirement. Students are not required to re-register at the University of Manitoba to receive prizes.
Applications are due by 11:59 p.m. on October 13, 2026.
Science Leadership Scholarships
The UM Science Students’ Association has established an endowment fund at the University of Manitoba to create annual leadership-based scholarships. The available annual income from this fund will be used to offer up to nine leadership-based scholarships of equal value in three distinct categories: community leadership, academic leadership and campus leadership.
For the 2026-27 academic year, the minimum value of each scholarship will be $1,650.
Eligibility
For all three categories, students must:
be enrolled full-time (minimum 80% course load) in the second, third or fourth year of study in any degree program in the Faculty of Science and
have achieved a minimum degree grade point average of 3.5.
Applicants will be required to submit a written statement (maximum 500 words) and two letters of reference to demonstrate how they meet the award criteria. For additional criteria, please see the application form.
All elected and appointed past and present SSA Councillors are ineligible for these scholarships.
Apply to Science Leadership Scholarships
Bernice Warkov Safeer Scholarship for Excellence in Mathematical Sciences
For the 2026-27 academic year, the value of this scholarship is $775.
Eligibility
The Bernice Warkov Safeer Scholarship for Excellence in Mathematical Sciences will be offered to a female undergraduate student who:
is enrolled full-time (minimum 80% course load) in the third year of either an honours program or a four-year major program in the mathematical sciences in the Faculty of Science
has achieved a minimum degree GPA of 3.5
has displayed excellence in one or more areas of the mathematical sciences (through coursework and/or independent study)
has shown herself to be a humanitarian with generosity of spirit and strength of character.
Eligible programs in the mathematical sciences include those individual and joint programs of the following departments: Actuarial Studies, Computer Science, Mathematics and Statistics.
Students will be required to provide written statements to demonstrate how they meet criteria (3) and (4).
Apply now
Microbiology Students’ Club (MiSC) Community Achievement Scholarship
For the 2026-27 academic year, the value of this scholarship is $1,200.
The Microbiology Student’s Club (MiSC) has established an annually funded award at the University of Manitoba. The purpose of this scholarship is to recognize undergraduate Microbiology, Biochemistry or Genetics students who are making significant contributions to the scientific community while maintaining academic success, as well as to encourage and support strong community involvement and leadership abilities. One scholarship with a value of $1,200 will be given to an undergraduate student who:
is enrolled full-time (minimum 80% course load) in any year of study in the Faculty of Science in either:
a Microbiology major, honours and/or Co-operative Option program;
a Biochemistry major, honours and/or Co-operative Option program;
a Genetics major, honours and/or Co-operative Option program;
has achieved a minimum degree grade point average of 3.0; and
has demonstrated strong community involvement and leadership abilities.
Applicants must submit a written statement (maximum 500 words) highlighting their contributions and connections to the scientific community, with an emphasis on the impact of their involvement.

Faculty of Science Fellowship for Graduate Excellence
2026 applications are now open and are due by 11:59 p.m. on Monday, November 30, 2026.
For 2026-2027, two awards will be available. One is designated for a master’s student and one for a PhD student.
Eligibility
Applicants must be full-time graduate students (not including pre-masters or occasional students) who are registered in the Faculty of Graduate Studies at the University of Manitoba in either the master’s or PhD program offered through the Faculty of Science.
Eligible candidates must have a minimum Grade Point Average (GPA) of 3.0 based on the last 60 credit hours (or equivalent) of their study.
Applicants must demonstrate exceptional research potential (for master’s students) or research achievement (for doctoral students).
Please note that this award has additional eligibility requirements. Further details will be provided on the application form.
Application process
Students must submit the application form along with a copy of their current transcripts and have two letters of reference submitted on the student’s behalf.
Evaluation

Graduate Science Research Scholarship for Indigenous Students
2026 applications are now open and are due by 11:59 p.m. on Monday, November 30, 2026.
For 2026-2027, one scholarship will be available to either a master’s or PhD student.
Eligibility
Applicants must self-declare as a First Nations, Métis or Inuit person from Canada.
Applicants must be enrolled full-time in the Faculty of Graduate Studies in any master's or doctoral program offered through the Faculty of Science at the University of Manitoba.
Eligible candidates must have a minimum grade point average of 3.0 based on the last 60 credit hours (or equivalent) of study.
Additionally, applicants must be conducting a research project with potential applications that may benefit Indigenous communities or address Indigenous affairs (for example, water quality, renewable energy, environmental health, internet accessibility, and more).
Candidates must self-declare as a First Nations, Métis or Inuit person from Canada.
Application process
Students must submit an application package, which consists of the following:
a description of the research proposal
copies of recent transcripts
two reference letters, one of which will be from the applicant’s current advisor
The reference letters must describe the student’s work experience and commitment to issues affecting Indigenous people.
Apply now
Molly Weinberg Soudack Scholarship for Women in Science
2026 applications are now open and are due by 11:59 p.m. on Monday, November 30, 2026.
For 2026-2027, one scholarship will be available to a woman pursuing a master’s degree.
Eligibility
Applicants must self-identify as a woman and be enrolled full-time in the Faculty of Graduate Studies in any year of any master’s program offered by the Faculty of Science at the University of Manitoba.
Eligible candidates must have a minimum grade point average of 3.5 based on the last 60 credit hours (or equivalent) of study.
To be eligible for this award, students must self-identify as a woman and have ancestral links to a Holocaust survivor or Residential School survivor.
Application process
Students must submit the application form along with a statement (maximum of 2 sentences) to self-declare that students meet the eligibility requirements.
Students must submit a copy of their current transcripts and have two letters of reference submitted on the student’s behalf.
Apply now
James C. Jamieson Graduate Scholarship in Biochemistry
2026 applications are now open and are due by 11:59 p.m. on Friday, November 6, 2026.
For 2026-2027, one scholarship will be available to either a master’s or PhD student.
In honour of Dr. James C. Jamieson, an endowment fund was established to reward the academic achievements of graduate students in the Faculty of Science pursuing studies in Biochemistry.
Eligibility
Applicants must be enrolled full-time in the Faculty of Graduate and Postdoctoral Studies in a Master’s or PhD program offered by the Faculty of Science.
Eligible candidates must have a minimum Grade Point Average (GPA) of 3.5 based on the last 60 credit hours (or equivalent) of their study.
Applicants must be undertaking research in an aspect of Biochemistry (i.e., involving biomolecules such as proteins, peptides, nucleic acids [DNA or RNA], carbohydrates, lipids, or membranes).
Applicants must demonstrate exceptional research potential (for master’s students) or research achievement (for doctoral students).
Application process
Students must submit the application form that includes a copy of their current transcripts.
Students must send a copy of their application to their supervisor and send them the Supervisor’s Assessment Form for them to complete on their behalf.

Graduate student conference support
Please note that requests made after the travel date will not be accepted.
Please note that conference travel funding is limited to twice per year, with the funding year running from April 1 through March 31.
Graduate students can apply for travel support from the Faculty of Science to attend conferences. To be eligible for conference travel, the student must:
be a registered graduate student in a department within the Faculty of Science,
be a co-author on the accepted paper or poster,
be the person presenting the work and
be a recipient of no more than two travel funding awards per year.
To apply for support, the student must first submit a request to their home department using the link below. Travel requests to the Faculty of Science must be made before the travel date. In all cases, support is provided as a reimbursement for incurred expenses, not as an upfront payment.

Student group funding
The Faculty of Science acknowledges the outstanding efforts of its student groups, as well as those external to the Faculty, in supporting Science students and fostering a sense of community. We recognize that the financial costs associated with these activities and events may sometimes exceed the budget of student groups.
To assist with these expenses, student groups may apply for funding from the Faculty of Science Dean's Office using the following form.
Submitting your request
The student group funding request form doesn't need to be completed in one sitting.
Timeline
Funding must be requested and approved in advance of the activity or event. Therefore, applications must be submitted at least two months before the activity or event.
How your request is evaluated
Some of the criteria used to evaluate requests include, but are not limited to:
the impact of an activity or event,
if the purpose or goals of the activity or event align with the Faculty of Science's mission and values,
clarity of budget,
cost per attendee,
other funding approved by other groups (SSA, UMSU),
the frequency of approved funding requests by the Faculty of Science Dean's Office
collaboration and partnerships,
past track record of managing funds, and
how the Faculty of Science would be recognized.
What happens next
All funding requests are reviewed by the Associate Dean (programs) and the Associate Dean (student experience).
Please note that we may not be able to fully support all requests. If funding is granted, the Dean's Office may either purchase items for the activity or event directly, or the student group may submit an invoice with receipts as proof of payment. Further details will be provided upon approval of the request.
